text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Pager: multi-region failover initiated — eu-west-1 partial AZ outage detected. Auto-DR kicked at 1718277123.

Alex Chen: On-call. Seeing spike in 5xx and timeouts for embedding and gen routes. Metrics show backend health flapping for eu-west-1. Paging network team.

Priya Nair: Network ops here. Initial checks: switch fabric in eu-west-1 reported packet loss and some asymmetric routing. Route53 health checks flagged instance failures, but some resolvers still resolve to eu-west-1 IPs due to cached answers. TTL was 30s.

Samir Patel: Any sign of autoscaler in eu-central or us-east warming up? We should shift capacity before we start dropping connections.

Alex Chen: Autoscale attempted to create warm hosts in eu-central but warm-pool logic didn't trigger because of a bug in the drain predicate. Logs:
```
Error: warm_pool_condition false for region eu-central - predicate matched draining=false but preferred_capacity=0
```

Marina Lopez: CS reporting a handful of large enterprise customers pinned to eu-west-1 are seeing high latency and timeouts. Opening high-priority tickets and drafting in-product status.

Route53 Bot: Alert: health-checks for eu-west-1 failed 6/6. Traffic policy indicates failover to eu-central but traffic still uneven due to EDNS stale cache.

Priya Nair: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Force weight to eu-central (Route53 policy override)
- Temporarily increase TTL to push resolvers to re-query? (note: increasing TTL won't help; lowering helps)
- Add edge translation to accept stale eu-west-1 host headers and proxy to eu-central

Alex Chen: Actions:
- Samir, please force-scale eu-central to target+40%: `infra/ops/force_scale --region eu-central --extra 40`
- Priya, change traffic weight now: `aws route53 change-traffic-policy-instance --id TP-334 --set-weight eu-central=100`
- Marina, send urgent note to affected customers.

Samir Patel: Running force-scale, ETA ~3:30 for instances to pass health checks. Starting warm-init scripts.

Alex Chen: Noting a nasty interaction: our internal session-affinity cookie includes origin-IP fingerprint. Since many edge resolvers still point to eu-west-1, sessions can bounce back and maintain stickiness to dead backends. We need to break affinity.

Priya Nair: Flushing sticky tables on proxies in front of eu-west-1 now: `curl -s -X POST http://proxy-eu-1.internal/flush` -> 200 OK. Also toggling LB affinity cookie to short-lived.

Route53 Bot: Change queued; propagation started. Monitoring DNS answers. Some corporate resolvers (ISP-level) still returning old A records.

Alex Chen: As a fallback, adding host-based rewrite on edge LBs to map stale eu-west-1 host IPs into the eu-central backend pool. Applying one node at a time.

Marina Lopez: Sent initial customer comms: short status, we9re routing to alternative region, ETA for mitigation 30-45m, please open support ticket if you have region-pinned configs.

Samir Patel: eu-central backends are coming up healthy 5/5. Traffic shift visible in metrics: ~85% now eu-central, residual 15% to eu-west-1. Error rate dropping from 12% to 1.8% over last 10m.

Alex Chen: Noted lingering issue: DNS caching causing split-brain routing for a subset of users. Host NAT workaround holding so far. Also saw one instance in eu-west stuck in deregistration; deregister API returned 504. Manually terminating that host.

Priya Nair: Opened ticket with cloud provider: case #CLOUD-8902. Posted traces, BGP dumps, and health-check failures. Asked for expedited network fabric RCA.

Incident Bot: :information_source: Mid-incident snapshot: failover triggered -> partial DNS cache retention -> session affinity causing backend loops -> host NAT and proxy flush applied -> autoscaler warmed eu-central -> mitigation progressing.

Marina Lopez: CS update: 5 customers with strict region pins impacted, all contacted. Offering SLA credits proactively.

Samir Patel: I'm going to add a post-mortem action to remove region-pin brittle configs from onboarding checklist and add a test that exercises DNS-based failover in CI.

Alex Chen: Handing off to night oncall at 1718279523 — Samir will take pager. Handoff notes:
- Status: mitigated, traffic ~98% eu-central, residual <2% to eu-west-1 via cached resolvers.
- Actions completed: forced Route53 weight, flushed proxy sticky tables, host NAT mapping, forced scale in eu-central, terminated stuck instance.
- Open items: cloud provider RCA, follow-up on warm-pool predicate bug, update runbook for TTL/EDNS caching guidance.

Samir Patel: Acknowledged. I9ll monitor and follow up on provider case. I9ll also ensure runbook contains steps to invalidate session affinity and to check deregistration timeouts.

Alex Chen: Closing active pager handover. Postmortem to be created: `doc/incidents/1718277123-postmortem.md`. Please add any logs or snippets you used into that doc. Thanks everyone. :pray:

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Thread closed by Alex Chen at 1718280723. Postmortem pending.
